governance.attested_by: miso23 cc-minload-premium 2026-06-29 (KEEPER on faithfulness grounds, supersedes miso22-offer-curve)
governance.note: One offer-SHAPE faithfulness lever on top of miso22 (all miso22/miso21 levers retained byte-for-byte: _MISO_OFFER_CURVE flat CC econ ramp + capped CT peak, export cap, firm imports, seam-flow/export limits, miso_pjm_border_anchor, coal mustrun/sync/sigmoid stack, cc/ct/st-gas intermediate splits). Correct the CC_REGULAR committed (min-stable-load) band from 0.92 to the measured part-load premium 1.20. GROUNDING: a CC's min-load $/MWh is ~30-40% above its full-load SRMC (measured CAMPD part-load shape; bin_assignments_MISO.csv cap-weighted CC_REGULAR HR 7.44), so the min-load tranche MUST price ABOVE the full-load body. 0.93x full-load incremental * 1.30 (low end of the premium) = 1.21; set 1.20, capped just under the ST_GAS non-inversion ceiling (ST_GAS committed 0.81*11.27 = 9.13 eff HR -> CC committed <= 9.13/7.44 = 1.227). The prior 0.92 (6.84 eff HR) sat BELOW CC econ_low (0.95*7.44 = 7.07) -- the inverse of the real part-load curve, an unphysical artificially-cheap min-load OFFER block. Lifting committed to 1.20 (8.93 eff HR) restores the correct part-load offer ORDER (committed > econ_high 1.08*7.44=8.0 > econ_low), with both CC committed and econ_high staying below ST_GAS min-load (9.1) and CT_PEAKER -- no merit inversion. Gated strictly on iso==MISO; ERCOT/PJM/CAISO/NYISO/NEISO/SPP resolved offer_curve_by_group verified byte-identical. NOT residual-fitted: this is an offer-shape correctness fix grounded in the measured part-load heat-rate curve, and it is METRIC-NEUTRAL (it makes the model MORE structurally faithful without being chosen for a fit gain -- claude.md #1).

model_miss_notes: The exceptions ledger is EMPTY by design: every out-of-tolerance criterion is a genuine MODEL MISS to fix in a later lever, NOT an accepted measured-input limitation, so the determination is honestly NOT-YET. miso23 is a faithfulness fix (correct CC min-load offer ordering) and is METRIC-NEUTRAL vs miso22 -- so the SAME misses remain, only marginally improved on the CC over-run. Measured authoritatively (gmModel, the dashboard/verdict basis -- NOT the raw dispatch klass sum, which folds in the BTM host-steam offset and would spuriously show a +7 TWh ST_GAS swing that is the fixed BTM subtraction, not a model change), the committed 0.92->1.20 move shifts gmModel CC_REGULAR -1.5/-0.8/-0.9 TWh (2023/24/25, the right direction on the over-run) and ST_GAS +0.1 / CT_PEAKER +0.1 / coal +0.3-0.7 / prices <$0.1/MWh -- i.e. metric-neutral. WHY metric-neutral: the committed band is a must-run min-load PRICE block whose VOLUME is set by the commitment decision, not by its own offer; raising its price corrects the merit ORDER (removing the unphysical below-body min-load block) without moving the volume. The residual misses, all MODEL MISS, are: (1) MERIT-ORDER SUBSTITUTION (the headline, UNCHANGED): model over-runs cheap CC_REGULAR (gmModel +24.2/+24.6/+12.7 vs EIA-923) and under-runs peakier CT_PEAKER (-19.6/-15.1/-16.6) and ST_GAS (-7.2/-9.5/-8.1). This is NOT offer-curve-addressable: CC's excess lives in its measured-FLAT econ body (econ_low 0.95 / econ_high 1.08 = the measured ~0.93x-avg incremental; steepening it to cut CC volume would be an unphysical fit to volume, rule #11), and CT's deficit is gated by the missing scarcity mechanism (see (4)) plus the import under-run (see (3)) -- the offer-curve committed/peak bands cannot move it. The defensible offer-curve work on this substitution is now exhausted; the next levers are import deliverability and reserve-demand co-optimization, not the gas offer curve. (2) 2025 DEAR-GAS COAL OVER-RUN: C2 system volume 2025 coal +12.2%, gas -11.6% (coal take-or-pay / PRB passthrough offer level in dear gas) -- the dominant 2025 miss, unaddressed by this lever. (3) IMPORT UNDER-RUN 2024/2025: net interchange model -17.0/-5.9 vs actual -23.1/-19.0 TWh -- MISO under-imports by ~6/~13 TWh (MISO's own LMP dual sits too close to the re-anchored PJM border to pull the full measured eastern transfer); the root cause that lets cheap domestic CC fill the gap and cannibalize CT/ST. A MISO-LMP-LEVEL item, separate from the offer curve. (4) PRICE TAIL / SCARCITY (C3c): 0 model >$200 hours vs 30/37/88 actual -- MISO's ELMP / Reserve Demand Curve (RDT) scarcity-pricing co-optimization is not yet modeled; the capped CT peak (4.0) is forward-correct but does not by itself create the tail. A separate reserve-demand lever. (5) 2025 STORAGE THROUGHPUT (C5b +1246%) carries over unchanged. Prices PASS C3a/C3b (avg 31.6/29.0/38.6, within tol) and fleet dispatch r PASSES C4; CO2 PASSES C5a. The determination is NOT-YET, decided by the C1/C2 hard gates above -- all honest MODEL MISSes, none reclassified to an accepted limitation.
